description: Cache Module Release Performance Gates — hard and soft guardrails for Phase 5 release sign-off.

hard_gates.description: L1 cache put p99 must not exceed 200 µs.
hard_gates.rationale: L1 put latency is on the critical query path; exceeding 200 µs causes SLO violations in high-throughput deployments.

hard_gates.description: L1 cache get (hit) p99 must not exceed 100 µs.
hard_gates.rationale: L1 hit latency must remain sub-millisecond for cache to provide meaningful benefit.

hard_gates.description: Tenant-isolation put p99 must not exceed 500 µs.
hard_gates.rationale: Tenant isolation must not impose more than 2.5× overhead vs plain put on the critical path.

hard_gates.description: Pattern-based invalidation p99 must not exceed 5 ms.
hard_gates.rationale: Invalidation operations must complete well before the next request cycle in high-frequency write workloads.

hard_gates.description: Concurrent read throughput must sustain ≥ 50 000 ops/s at benchmark thread settings.
hard_gates.rationale: Cache must scale to concurrent readers without lock contention degrading throughput below production demand.

hard_gates.description: Embedding cache query p99 must not exceed 500 µs.
hard_gates.rationale: Embedding cache is on the LLM inference critical path; latency above 500 µs degrades end-to-end LLM query response times.

soft_gates.description: Cache miss latency p99 should stay below 50 µs.
soft_gates.rationale: High miss latency indicates hash-map contention or an oversized L1 that slows lookups.

soft_gates.description: Mixed read/write throughput should sustain ≥ 30 000 ops/s.
soft_gates.rationale: Mixed workload is the realistic production scenario; soft gate catches lock-contention regressions early.

soft_gates.description: Warmup-from-log p99 should complete within 500 ms for a standard-sized log.
soft_gates.rationale: Slow warmup delays post-restart hit-rate recovery in production deployments.

soft_gates.description: Embedding batch store p99 should not exceed 10 ms for a standard batch.
soft_gates.rationale: Batch store latency impacts offline model inference pipelines.

manifest_completeness.policy: All listed benchmark IDs must be present in the release run output. A missing ID is treated as a blocking gate failure (GATE-CG-3 from PERFORMANCE_EXPECTATIONS.md).

known_limitations: RocksDB L3 benchmarks require a local RocksDB installation; they cannot run in environments without librocksdb-dev. In such environments, L3-dependent benchmark cases are skipped and must be explicitly marked as skipped (not missing) in the release evidence.
Redis coordinator benchmarks require a reachable Redis endpoint; they are skipped in environments without Redis connectivity. Skips must be documented in the release gate report.
Benchmark results on shared CI runners may show higher variance than on pinned hardware; variance > 10% CV should trigger a re-run on dedicated hardware before blocking a release.
Embedding cache benchmarks depend on the vector index stub implementation until real ANN backends are wired; results reflect stub latency and must be re-baselined when real backends land.
